_purpose: Products never offered as a RECOMMENDATION, because they are formulated for children (Luneth 2026-07-16: "no adult is ever going to take those… kids will never use our app"). Editorial CURATION config — OURS, not a Wallach claim and not a pillar projection — so it lives here hand-authored (manifest 'accounted') rather than derived. It changes only what we SHOW; it never touches a target, a dose, or a composition.
_scope: Excluded from EVERY recommendation/suggestion surface: the Coverage recommendations, condition pages, and the element/entity detail view's BEST SOURCES. The ONE place they remain fully present is the products database (the Knowledge drawer's Products tab), where they stay discoverable — that surface reads essentialSlugsByProduct(), which is deliberately NOT filtered. Enforced by the `kids_products_not_recommended` invariant.
_the_line_luneth_drew: FORMULATED for children — not merely MARKETED to them. Ruled 2026-07-16 when he cut cheri-mins + strawberry-kiwi-mins from a proposed 4: their copy is explicitly kid-directed ("No more tantrums… back to playtime"), but they ARE the adult Plant Derived Minerals composition — chemically identical to the adult bottle, adult-looking single-column labels — so an adult can take them and they earn their place in a recommendation. His words: "cheri-mins and strawberry-kiwi-mins are not kids products." ★ THE TEST IS THE FORMULA, NOT THE ADVERTISING. Claude proposed those two ON marketing copy and was overruled; a future session must not re-add them by re-reading that copy.
_evidence_note: Identified from Youngevity's own product copy + label panels — NEVER from the product NAME. A name heuristic was rejected because it both over- and under-fires: 'Kidney & Bladder Support' matches 'kid'; 'FlexeoPlus' says 'grandkids' (a product FOR grandparents); and 'Toddy' is a drink name, not 'toddler' (Ultra Body Toddy and Cal Toddy are ADULT — Luneth's own correction, 2026-07-16: "I misunderstood what 'toddy' means… it apparently is a type of drink, that is my mistake"). Verified 2026-07-16 by reading all 217 label images (only kids-toddy's panel is age-banded) and sweeping all 215 marketing descriptions.
_names_deliberately_absent: Only product_id is stored. The display name lives in the Products pillar and is resolved from it; re-storing it here would be a second home for a pillar fact that silently drifts if Youngevity renames a product (R3). The gate resolves every id below against eden/products/products.json and REDs on an unknown one — a typo cannot silently un-exclude a kids product.

excluded.evidence: FORMULATED for children — the label doses by AGE BAND: two %DV columns, "1/2 fl. oz. (Ages 1-3)" and "1 fl. oz. (Ages >=4)", with the child-calorie footnote "based on a 1,000 calorie diet for children 1-3 years of age". The ONLY age-banded panel among all 217 labels, i.e. the dosing axis itself is age. Pediatric-scale actives corroborate (Calcium 10 mg, Magnesium 5 mg) against the adult negative control Ultra Body Toddy (B-12 at 8333% DV). YGY copy agrees: supports "your child's development from their first year" through "their early teen years".

FORMULATED for children — YGY copy states the formulation directly: "formulated to provide children with a variety of nutrients needed for healthy growth and optimal health" (and "Do your kids HATE taking their vitamins?"). It is its own distinct powder formula, not an adult composition re-marketed. Its LABEL is single-column on the ordinary adult 2,000-calorie basis, so the panel alone does not settle it — read + arithmetically checked against both FDA DV tables 2026-07-16 (it matches the ages-4+ table 12/12), which rules out an ages-1-3 formula but not a kids product. The stated formulation is the evidence.

_considered_and_kept: Reviewed and deliberately NOT excluded, recorded so a future session sees they were examined rather than missed. (1) cheri-mins + strawberry-kiwi-mins — kid-MARKETED but ARE the adult Plant Derived Minerals formula; Luneth's explicit ruling 2026-07-16 (see _the_line_luneth_drew). (2) ultra-body-toddy + cal-toddy — 'Toddy' is a drink name, both adult, both confirmed by label. (3) The DUAL-AUDIENCE three, each naming adults outright: bone-building-formula ("helps teens and young adult women"), sta-clear ("formulated for teenagers and adults"), ultimate-multi-efa ("the optimal health of adults and children"). (4) Name false-positives that are ADULT: kidney-bladder-support ('Kidney'), flexeoplus ('grandkids' — a product FOR grandparents), ultimate-super-kb / sweet-eze ('kidney').
